title: Best Time to Visit Rajaji National Park: Seasons, Zones and Timings
seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Rajaji National Park | Season Guide
summary: The best time to visit Rajaji National Park, zone by zone: opening dates, Jhilmil Jheel's earlier season, safari timings and why winter suits birders.
content:
The best time to visit Rajaji National Park depends on which safari zone you choose. Most of the jeep safari zones follow one season, Jhilmil Jheel follows another, and Gohri Range is open for most of the year. This guide sets out the opening periods, the morning and evening entry timings, and what each part of the season offers, using the figures published for each zone.

## When Rajaji National Park is open

Chilla, Motichur, Ranipur and Mohand–Chillawali are generally open from 15 November to 15 June. They remain closed during the monsoon season. Opening and closing dates can move depending on Forest Department regulations, weather conditions and local management decisions, so check the dates for your trip before you make travel plans.

Many of Rajaji's seasonal streams stay dry for much of the year but turn into fast-flowing torrents during the monsoon.

### Jhilmil Jheel has a different season

Jhilmil Jheel Conservation Reserve, on the left bank of the Ganga in Haridwar District, is generally open for safari tourism during the October to June season. Its published entry timings begin on 15 October, a month before the main zones open, which makes it an option for visitors travelling in late October or early November.

### Gohri Range is open for most of the year

Gohri Range is generally open throughout the year except during August and September. Even so, year-round opening should not be treated as guaranteed. Monsoon conditions, route-specific permissions and Forest Department regulations can still affect safaris there.

## Morning and evening safari timings

The main zones run a morning slot and an afternoon/evening slot. The entry timings change three times during the season:

- **15 November to 15 February:** morning 6:30 AM to 8:00 AM, afternoon 1:30 PM to 3:00 PM
- **16 February to 15 April:** morning 6:00 AM to 7:30 AM, afternoon 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM
- **16 April to 15 June:** morning 5:30 AM to 7:00 AM, afternoon 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM

Jhilmil Jheel publishes its own entry periods:

- **15 October to 31 January:** morning 7:00 AM to 10:00 AM, evening 2:00 PM to 4:30 PM
- **1 February to 31 March:** morning 6:30 AM to 9:00 AM, evening 2:30 PM to 4:30 PM
- **1 April to 30 June:** morning 6:00 AM to 9:00 AM, evening 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM

Gohri Range lists indicative safari timings of 6:30 AM to 9:00 AM in the morning and 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM in the evening.

A typical jeep safari lasts about 2.5 to 3 hours, depending on the zone, route and conditions. Plan to reach the gate at least 20 minutes before the reporting or last-entry time printed on your permit or booking confirmation. Timings can be revised by the Forest Department, so the time on your permit is the one to follow.

### Morning or evening: which slot to choose

Early morning safaris can offer good chances to watch wildlife, particularly when animals are moving along forest tracks and open areas. For birdwatchers, early morning is generally a productive period because bird activity is often higher during the cooler hours. At Gohri, both early morning and late afternoon can be good times, when animals are more active.

The morning is also when the Chilla elephant safari runs. It is an early-morning experience of about 1 to 1.5 hours, subject to availability and Forest Department arrangements.

The afternoon slot suits visitors who cannot manage a very early start, especially later in the season when morning entry moves to 5:30 AM. Whichever slot you pick, sightings are never guaranteed. They depend on animal movement, season, weather and habitat conditions.

## Best time to visit Rajaji National Park by season

### November to February: winter birdwatching

Winter is particularly rewarding for bird watchers. Rajaji has more than 300 recorded bird species, including resident birds, winter migrants and altitudinal visitors, and winter brings additional migratory species to suitable habitats, wetlands and water bodies. At Jhilmil Jheel, winter coincides with the presence of many migratory birds in the wider Jhilmil–Ganga landscape, and a Forest Department preliminary checklist records 238 bird species in the reserve.

Mornings can be cool in winter, so carry a light jacket for an early safari.

### October to April at Jhilmil Jheel

For Jhilmil Jheel, the October to April period is particularly attractive if you want pleasant weather, wetland landscapes and birdwatching. Conditions for wildlife photography there vary with season, water availability, temperature and animal movement.

### Outside winter

Bird watching does not stop when the migrants leave. Other seasons offer chances to see resident birds, breeding activity and seasonal changes in bird behaviour. The best time for you depends on the species you hope to see, the weather and permitted access.

## Book early for weekends and holidays

Safari vehicles and permits are limited, and demand can be higher than the number of vehicles available. Advance booking is recommended for weekends, public holidays, winter holidays and other peak travel periods, especially if you want a particular date or the morning slot.

Once you have chosen your dates and zone, check availability and send your request through our booking page. Our team will confirm the slot, permit details and reporting time for your visit.

title: Chilla vs Jhilmil Jheel: Which Rajaji Safari Zone Suits You?
seoTitle: Chilla vs Jhilmil Jheel: Which Rajaji Safari Zone?
summary: Chilla or Jhilmil Jheel? Compare landscape, wildlife, distance from Haridwar, season and timings to choose the right Rajaji jeep safari zone for your trip.
content:
Chilla and Jhilmil Jheel are both close to Haridwar, and both can be booked as Rajaji jeep safari zones. They are very different trips, though. Chilla is a forest, grassland and river safari in Rajaji National Park. Jhilmil Jheel is a wetland and grassland Conservation Reserve known for Swamp Deer and birds. This Chilla vs Jhilmil Jheel comparison covers landscape, wildlife, access and season so you can pick the one that fits your trip.

## Chilla vs Jhilmil Jheel at a glance

- **Chilla landscape:** Sal forests, open grasslands and riverine habitats
- **Jhilmil Jheel landscape:** wetlands, grasslands, riverine habitats, forest patches and scrubland
- **Chilla location:** on the Haridwar–Rishikesh bypass road, about 10 km from Haridwar and 20 km from Rishikesh
- **Jhilmil Jheel location:** on the left bank of the Ganga in Haridwar District, about 20 km from Haridwar
- **Season:** Chilla is generally open 15 November to 15 June; Jhilmil Jheel is generally open October to June
- **Safari length:** about 2 hours 30 minutes at Chilla; about 2 to 2.5 hours at Jhilmil Jheel

## Landscape

### Chilla

Chilla combines dense Sal forest, open grassland and riverine habitat linked to the Chilla area and the Ganga. The jeep safari follows a route of about 2 hours 30 minutes through forest around Mundal, Mithawali and Khara, and the circular route, where it applies, is about 36 km. Short halts at the Mundal and Ghasiram machans (watchtowers) give you a view over the surrounding forest.

The Chilla Complex also has an Interpretation Centre and Library, useful if you want to learn about the area's wildlife, forests and conservation.

### Jhilmil Jheel

Jhilmil Jheel Conservation Reserve was declared in 2005 and covers about 37.84 sq km in the Chiriyapur forest landscape. It is a mosaic of wetlands, grasslands, riverine habitats, tropical mixed moist deciduous forest and scrubland. The wetland includes old river channels, seasonal and perennial marshes and an oxbow-lake system associated with the Ganga. Designated observation areas and watchtowers may be used for wildlife and bird watching, subject to Forest Department regulations and local conditions.

## Wildlife

### What you may see at Chilla

Chilla's mix of habitats supports a broad range of species. Visitors may encounter:

- **Big cats:** Bengal Tiger, Leopard
- **Large mammals:** Asian Elephant, Wild Boar, Sloth Bear
- **Deer:** Chital (Spotted Deer), Sambar, Barking Deer
- **Primates:** Hanuman Langur, Rhesus Macaque
- **Birds:** Great Hornbill, kingfishers, eagles, peafowl, quails, falcons, vultures and many other forest and riverine birds

### What you may see at Jhilmil Jheel

Jhilmil Jheel is recognised as an important habitat in Uttarakhand for the Swamp Deer (Barasingha). The reserve also supports Asian Elephants, Spotted Deer, Sambar, Wild Boar, Nilgai and Leopard.

Birdlife is the other big draw. A preliminary checklist published by the Uttarakhand Forest Department recorded 238 bird species here, including wetland birds, waders, raptors, forest birds and other resident and migratory species. Depending on the season and water conditions, you may see kingfishers, waterbirds, waders, raptors, woodpeckers, flycatchers and larks.

At both zones, sightings are natural encounters and cannot be guaranteed.

## Access and gate location

Chilla is reached from Rishikesh, Haridwar and Dehradun via the Chilla Power Channel Road. By road it is about 10 km from Haridwar, 20 km from Rishikesh, about 40 km from Dehradun and about 35 km from Jolly Grant Airport. The nearest major railway station is Haridwar.

Jhilmil Jheel lies along the Haridwar–Najibabad road corridor, about 20 km from Haridwar. The nearest railway station is Haridwar Junction and the nearest airport is Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun. Access arrangements at Jhilmil can change, so confirm the current entry point and reporting location before you travel.

## Season and timings

Chilla is generally open from 15 November to 15 June and closes for the monsoon. Morning slots fall between 5:30 AM and 8:00 AM depending on the month, and afternoon slots between 1:30 PM and 4:30 PM.

Jhilmil Jheel is generally open from October to June, with its first published entry period starting on 15 October. Its winter morning entry is later, from 7:00 AM to 10:00 AM between 15 October and 31 January. The October to April period is particularly attractive for pleasant weather, wetland landscapes and birdwatching.

## Extras and costs

Chilla offers an elephant safari in addition to the jeep safari, subject to availability and Forest Department arrangements. It is an early-morning experience of about 1 to 1.5 hours.

Gypsy hire is ₹3,500 per vehicle at both zones. Entry charges are structured differently: Chilla uses the standard Rajaji park entry fee and vehicle permit, while Jhilmil Jheel has its own entry ticket and permit fee.

## Which one should you choose?

- **Choose Chilla** if you want forest, grassland and river scenery in one drive, hope to see elephants and a wide range of mammals, or want to add an elephant safari.
- **Choose Jhilmil Jheel** if you are a birdwatcher, want to look for Swamp Deer, or prefer wetland landscapes.
- **Travelling between 15 October and 15 November?** Jhilmil Jheel's season starts before Chilla's.
- **Coming from Rishikesh?** Chilla is the closer of the two.

Both zones can be booked through our booking page. Tell us your date, number of visitors and preferred slot, and our team will confirm availability for Chilla or Jhilmil Jheel.

title: Rajaji Safari Booking: How to Book a Jeep Safari Step by Step
seoTitle: Rajaji Safari Booking: Step-by-Step Jeep Safari Guide
summary: Rajaji safari booking step by step: the visitor details and ID you need, how confirmation works, gate reporting times, and the cancellation and refund rules.
content:
Rajaji safari booking is simple once you know what the Forest Department needs from you. Permits are processed with each visitor's details, vehicles are limited, and timings are strict at the gate. This guide walks through each step, the documents to carry, and the cancellation and refund points to read before you pay.

## Before you start

Have these details ready:

- **Travel date and slot:** morning or afternoon/evening, subject to availability in your chosen zone
- **Safari zone:** for example Chilla, Motichur, Ranipur, Mohand–Chillawali, Jhilmil Jheel or Gohri
- **Visitor details:** full name, age and gender of every traveller
- **Identity documents:** valid ID for each visitor; foreign nationals may be asked for passport details
- **Group size:** a gypsy takes up to 6 persons

Advance booking is recommended for weekends, public holidays and peak tourist periods, because demand can exceed the number of vehicles available.

## Rajaji safari booking step by step

### Step 1: Choose your date, slot and zone

Pick your date and your preferred slot. Zone availability depends on the season, forest regulations and permit quotas. Chilla, Motichur, Ranipur and Mohand–Chillawali are generally open from 15 November to 15 June. Jhilmil Jheel is generally open from October to June, and Gohri Range is generally open all year except August and September. At Chilla you can also ask about the early-morning elephant safari, which runs subject to availability.

### Step 2: Share visitor details

Give the name, age and gender of every traveller, along with their identity document details. These are needed for permit processing. Children above 11 years are charged the applicable park entry fee.

### Step 3: Submit your booking request

Fill in the booking form on our website with your preferred date, zone, number of visitors and contact details. If you would rather speak to someone, the booking team is on +91 98298 50501, +91 93765 91390 and +91 99829 07130.

### Step 4: Complete the payment

Pay the applicable safari and booking charges as advised during booking. Entry fees, gypsy hire and guide fees are separate charges.

### Step 5: Receive your confirmation

After confirmation, the booking details, reporting location, contact information and permit information, where applicable, are shared by email or WhatsApp. You should get your booking confirmation within the hour, subject to permit availability.

### Step 6: Reach the gate on time

Reach the designated entry gate before the reporting time on your permit or booking confirmation. Carry the booking confirmation and your original identity documents, and follow the instructions of the Rajaji Tiger Reserve and Forest Department staff.

## Safari timings and reporting

For Chilla, Motichur, Ranipur and Mohand–Chillawali, the entry timings change with the season:

- **15 November to 15 February:** morning 6:30 AM to 8:00 AM, afternoon 1:30 PM to 3:00 PM
- **16 February to 15 April:** morning 6:00 AM to 7:30 AM, afternoon 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM
- **16 April to 15 June:** morning 5:30 AM to 7:00 AM, afternoon 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM

Jhilmil Jheel and Gohri Range publish their own timings, and our team will confirm the right one for your zone. A typical jeep safari lasts about 2.5 to 3 hours.

The most important rule is to arrive at the gate at least 20 minutes before the reporting or last-entry time on your permit. Guests who arrive after the permitted time may be denied entry, and in that case the safari fee is not refundable. Before you travel, check the final date, timing, zone and reporting details on your permit or booking confirmation.

## Cancellation, changes and refunds

Read these points before you pay:

- **Changes after the permit is issued:** changes to the safari date, slot or zone may not be permitted, subject to the rules of the Forest Department.
- **Cancellations and refunds:** any cancellation, change or refund request is handled strictly according to the Forest Department and park rules and the terms of the booking. Where those rules do not allow a refund or change, no refund is given.
- **Cancellations beyond our control:** if a safari is cancelled, suspended or does not run because of natural calamities, adverse weather, government or Forest Department restrictions, wildlife safety concerns or park closure, no refund is provided.
- **Late arrival:** entry may be refused and the safari fee is not refundable.

## Other terms worth knowing

- **Nature guide:** an authorised nature guide is mandatory with each safari vehicle wherever park and Forest Department rules require one.
- **Student concession:** available only for recognised institutional educational tours, subject to Forest Department rules, eligibility and approval.
- **Inside the park:** do not leave the vehicle except at designated points, do not smoke or light fires, and do not carry firearms. Alcohol and non-vegetarian food are not permitted.
- **Sightings:** wildlife sightings are not guaranteed and depend on animal movement, season, weather and habitat conditions.

This is a private booking assistance service, not an official government website. All permits, fees and operating conditions are subject to the approval of the Forest Department authorities.

When your details are ready, send your request through our booking page and our team will check availability for your date and zone.

title: Rajaji Jeep Safari Price and Entry Fees Explained
seoTitle: Rajaji Jeep Safari Price and Entry Fees Explained
summary: Rajaji jeep safari price explained: park entry fees, vehicle permits, gypsy hire, guide and elephant ride charges, Jhilmil Jheel fees and filming charges.
content:
The Rajaji jeep safari price is not one single ticket. Your total is built from a park entry fee for each visitor, a vehicle permit, the gypsy hire and, if you want one, a guide. This post sets out the figures in the published Tickets, Entry Fees and Safari Charges list so you can work out your own cost.

Fees are set by the Forest Department and can change without prior notice. Treat the figures below as a reference and confirm the current rates when you book.

## Park entry fee

This applies at Chilla, Haridwar/Ranipur, Motichur and Chillawali/Mohand:

- **Indian visitors:** ₹150 per person
- **Foreign visitors:** ₹600 per person

Children above 11 years are charged the applicable park entry fee.

## Vehicle or jeep permit

- **Indian visitors:** ₹250 per vehicle
- **Foreign visitors:** ₹500 per vehicle

## Rajaji jeep safari price: gypsy hire

The gypsy safari cost is set per gate, and vehicle hire is separate from the entry and permit charges.

- **Chilla, Motichur, Ranipur and Mohand–Chillawali:** ₹3,500 per vehicle
- **Jhilmil Jheel:** ₹3,500 per vehicle
- **Gohri Range:** ₹3,500 per vehicle
- **Indicative hire for Indian visitors:** ₹3,500 per vehicle
- **Indicative hire for foreign visitors:** ₹3,500 to ₹4,000 per vehicle
- **Maximum capacity:** up to 6 persons per vehicle, subject to applicable rules

After obtaining the entry permit, visitors pay the jeep safari fare at their selected entry gate. A typical safari lasts about 2.5 to 3 hours, depending on the zone, route and conditions.

## Jhilmil Jheel entry charges

Jhilmil Jheel is not in the park entry list above. It has its own entry ticket and permit charges:

- **Indian visitors:** ₹200 per person
- **Indian permit fee:** ₹300
- **Foreign visitors:** ₹800 per person
- **Foreign permit fee:** ₹400

## Guide charges

A trained nature guide can tell you about the forest, wildlife, birds, habitats and local biodiversity during the safari. Guide fees vary by safari zone, guide category and applicable rules.

- **General guide (if needed):** ₹1,000
- **Experienced bird and wildlife guide:** ₹1,200 to ₹1,800

Where the Forest Department or a particular zone requires a guide, visitors must follow that rule.

## Elephant ride

The elephant ride is an early-morning option, subject to availability.

- **Indian visitors:** approximately ₹1,200 to ₹1,500
- **Foreign visitors:** a higher rate, to be confirmed at the gate

## Photography and filming fees

Photography and commercial filming inside protected areas may need prior permission and the applicable fees.

- **Fixed or movie camera, non-commercial:** no fee for Indian or foreign visitors
- **Movie camera or video, commercial:** ₹500 Indian, ₹1,500 foreign
- **Feature film, filming fee per day:** ₹1,00,000 Indian, ₹2,00,000 foreign
- **Documentary film, filming fee per day:** ₹10,000 Indian, ₹30,000 foreign
- **Refundable security money, feature film:** ₹1,00,000 Indian, ₹2,00,000 foreign, per film
- **Refundable security money, documentary film:** ₹50,000 Indian, ₹1,00,000 foreign, per film

## How to work out your total

Add up these parts:

- **Entry:** the per-person entry fee for every visitor, or Jhilmil Jheel's own ticket and permit
- **Permit:** one vehicle permit for each gypsy in the main zones
- **Vehicle:** the gypsy hire for each vehicle
- **Guide:** a guide fee, if you take a guide or the zone requires one
- **Extras:** an elephant ride, if one is available and you book it

A group of up to six people can share one gypsy, so the vehicle costs are split across the group. Entry, gypsy hire and guide fees are always separate charges.

## Concessions

Student concessions are available only for recognised institutional educational tours, subject to Forest Department rules, eligibility and approval.

## Book early in peak periods

Safari vehicles and permits are subject to availability. Advance booking is recommended for weekends, public holidays and peak tourist periods, as demand can exceed the number of vehicles.

Fees are set by the Forest Department and can change at any time. When you book through our booking page, our team will confirm the current charges for your date, zone and group before you pay.

title: Rajaji Safari from Rishikesh or Haridwar: Nearest Gates and Zones
seoTitle: Rajaji Safari from Rishikesh or Haridwar: Nearest Gates
summary: Planning a Rajaji safari from Rishikesh or Haridwar? See the nearest gates and zones, road distances, train and airport options, and reporting time tips.
content:
Most visitors plan a Rajaji safari from Rishikesh or Haridwar, and both cities are close to several safari gates. The right gate depends on where you are staying, how early you can leave and what kind of forest you want to see. This guide lists the zones nearest to each city, using the distances published for each zone.

## Rajaji safari from Haridwar

Haridwar has the widest choice of nearby gates:

- **Motichur:** about 9 km
- **Chilla:** 10 km
- **Jhilmil Jheel:** about 20 km, along the Haridwar–Najibabad road corridor
- **Ranipur Gate:** close to the Ranipur and BHEL area, with convenient road access from Haridwar
- **Mohand Gate (Chillawali):** about 35 to 40 km

### Ranipur Gate, the Haridwar Zone

The Haridwar Zone is entered through Ranipur Gate. The safari covers a route of about 25 km in roughly 2 hours, through mixed forest, open grassland patches, small hills and seasonal streams. Visitors may see Asian Elephants, Spotted Deer, Sambar, Nilgai, Barking Deer and Wild Boar, and leopards occur in the wider forest. It is a practical choice if you are staying in Haridwar, and it fits well with visits to Har Ki Pauri, Mansa Devi Temple, Chandi Devi Temple or the Sureshwari Devi Temple near Ranipur.

### Chilla and Jhilmil Jheel

Chilla sits on the Haridwar–Rishikesh bypass road and offers Sal forest, grassland and riverine habitat, with an early-morning elephant safari where available. Jhilmil Jheel lies on the left bank of the Ganga in Haridwar District and is known for Swamp Deer (Barasingha) and birdlife. Its season runs from October to June, so it is an option before the main zones open on 15 November.

## Rajaji safari from Rishikesh

From Rishikesh, two zones are about the same distance away:

- **Chilla:** 20 km, reached via the Chilla Power Channel Road
- **Motichur:** about 20 km, along the Haridwar–Rishikesh route
- **Ranipur Gate:** about 35 to 40 km, depending on the route
- **Mohand Gate (Chillawali):** about 40 km

### Chilla from Rishikesh

Chilla is one of the most popular safari areas of Rajaji and is accessible from both Haridwar and Rishikesh. The jeep route takes about 2 hours 30 minutes through forest around Mundal, Mithawali and Khara, with short halts at the Mundal and Ghasiram machans.

### Motichur from Rishikesh

Motichur was one of the former wildlife sanctuaries that, with Rajaji and Chilla, became Rajaji National Park in 1983. Its safari follows a circular route of about 25 km through Sal forest and open clearings, where you may see Asian Elephant, Chital, Sambar, Barking Deer, Wild Boar and Hanuman Langur.

### Gohri Range

Gohri Range, in the buffer zone landscape of Rajaji Tiger Reserve, is offered as a quieter jungle safari near Rishikesh and Haridwar. It is generally open all year except August and September. Our team confirms the reporting point when you book.

## Coming from Dehradun or Delhi

- **Mohand Gate (Chillawali):** about 25 to 30 km from Dehradun, near Ganeshpur on the Dehradun–Haridwar highway
- **Motichur:** about 35 km from Dehradun
- **Chilla:** about 40 km from Dehradun
- **Ranipur Gate:** about 55 to 60 km from Dehradun
- **From Delhi:** Chilla and Motichur are about 224 km via NH 334, Ranipur about 250 km and Mohand about 251 km

The road route from Delhi to Chilla runs via Meerut, Khatauli, Muzaffarnagar, Roorkee and Haridwar.

## Trains and flights

- **Haridwar Railway Station:** the nearest major station for Chilla, Ranipur and Jhilmil Jheel
- **Motichur:** nearby stations include Motichur, Raiwala, Haridwar and Rishikesh
- **Mohand Gate:** the nearest stations are Dehradun, Saharanpur and Roorkee
- **Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun:** about 35 km from Chilla and Motichur, 45 to 50 km from Ranipur and about 48 km from Mohand Gate

## Plan around the reporting time

Morning entry can be as early as 5:30 AM between 16 April and 15 June, and you need to be at the gate at least 20 minutes before the reporting or last-entry time on your permit. If you are staying in Rishikesh or Haridwar and want a morning slot, a gate close to your hotel makes the early start easier. If you are travelling a longer distance, an afternoon slot may suit you better.

Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed at any gate. They depend on animal movement, season, weather and habitat conditions.

Tell us where you are staying when you book through our booking page, and our team can suggest the nearest available zone for your date.
